rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read
rules_evaluated.evidence: All definite references resolve. 'the bug you brought from prework' (chunk 0), 'the diff' (introduced chunk 1 'show me the diff', reused chunk 2), 'the compound step' (named chunk 0 as 'The compound move', reused chunk 2 same-file carve-out), 'the fix'/'the change' (session artifact, chunk 3) all hold under sequential read. 'the contract' (chunk 3, Optional bullet) is generic TDD vocabulary ('the test names the contract'), not a deck-internal pointer with competing candidates — not a referent-tracking case. 'the PR' previewed in chunk-0 chrome before being produced is covered by the explicit session-artifact carve-out, which does not require the artifact to already exist at first mention.

Only one cross-beat pointer: chunk 5 'Hand off to the ticket close.' Names the target by its content/function (closing the ticket), not by relative position ('the next exercise'), satisfying the title-or-claim requirement. Chunk-0 forward mention of the compound move is likewise named by content ('writing down what you learned... once the ticket's closed'), not position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-derived from scratch against curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md's include order: orient-and-introspect -> fix-tests-first -> close-the-ticket -> compound-and-close. Chunk 0's reworded claim ('The compound move... comes later in the module, once the ticket's closed') now correctly states compound-and-close (Ex4) follows close-the-ticket (Ex3) — no contradiction with the actual order. This is the line the prior instance flagged (title-slide claim placing compound 'in the next exercise'); the current wording no longer makes that positional claim and matches the real sequence. Chunk 2's forward reference to 'the compound step' and chunk 5's 'the ticket close' both resolve against real beats in the module's Key Concepts ('orient -> fix -> close -> compound') and include list.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the file (no 'take a guess' / 'what do you think' followed by a narrated outcome). Rule does not apply to this file's content.

Every chunk carries at least one self-standing claim. Chunk 4 (single-bullet declaration slide) is substantive — a claim plus explanation plus a guidance line, not a bare wait-state — and is explicitly attested as deliberate in the maintainer block's 2026-08-07 note.

Every header's content matches its chunk body: 'Write the failing test and fix the root cause' (chunk 1), 'Read the diff and push back on a line' (chunk 2), 'Interrogate the fix for a deeper layer' (chunk 3), 'There is always a next plausible answer' (chunk 4, matched near-verbatim by 'There will be a next plausible answer...'), 'Ship the PR' (chunk 5, commit/push/PR content). Chunk 4's header-truth guard holds: body says 'will always try to find', never 'finds' — matches the maintainer's do-not-strengthen accept-note.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-cadence caps (aggregate: Not-X-Not-Y-Z, anaphora triples, self-grading superlatives, number+retraction, abstraction-noun stacks, empty-leg verb triplets)
rules_evaluated.evidence: Scanned all six chunks against every sub-item: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction, no anaphora/epistrophe triples, no self-grading superlatives (no 'one of the most useful' or similar value-prop leak), no bare number-then-retraction ('25 minutes' is exact Time chrome, not a hedged figure), no abstraction-noun stacks, no verb triplets with an empty leg. Self-grading-superlative sub-item (the one blocking sub-item within this rule) specifically clean.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide
rules_evaluated.evidence: No repo-internal terms (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun) appear. 'move' ('the compound move', 'this exact move') and 'compound' are the training's own established arc vocabulary (getting-going.md Key Concepts: 'The loop is orient -> fix -> close -> compound'), not maintainer meta-dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles only, go very lightly
rules_evaluated.evidence: Matches the maintainer-documented 2026-07-09 emphasis pass exactly: single non-chrome bold handle 'Tests-first, root-cause-driven' at its naming moment (chunk 1); blockquote callout 'Small fix, small test' bold is the explicitly exempted callout; widget chrome labels (Time/What you do/What you build/The point/What happened/Optional) bold as chrome, not counted. Chunk 4 (declaration slide) carries zero bold, matching the maintainer's 'No bold; the file keeps its single handle' note.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position computed, content ordinals linted
rules_evaluated.evidence: File uses no '## Phase N:' or '## N.' step headers and no in-body 'Step K'/'Phase K' references requiring renumber-tracking. Section headers are plain imperative/declaration titles with no hand-numbering. Rule does not apply.
